THIS CRIMINAL PETITION, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER 1.

The petitioner is before this Court seeking for the following relief:
a. Quash the entire proceedings in PCR No. 20/2018 filed by the respondent No.2 on the file of II Additional Senior Civil Judge and CJM Court Mangalore registered in Crime No.13/2018 by the Respondent Police against the petitioners for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 463, 468 r/w 34 of IPC b.
Grant such other and further reliefs as this Hon'ble Court deems fit and proper under the facts and circumstances of the case in the interest of justice and equity.

2. The respondent-Bank had filed a private complaint in PC No.20/2018 under Section 200 of the Cr.P.C. for offenses punishable under Section 420, 463, 468 read with 34 of the IPC.
3.

In the said complaint, it is alleged that the petitioner who is accused No.2 therein, in collusion with accused No.1-Manager of the complainant Bank, had fabricated records on which basis a loan came to be NC: 2024:KHC:10270 sanctioned to an amount of Rs.25,00,000/- to accused No.2,
which in turn was transferred to a third party and not used for the purpose which the loan was granted.

The documentation which has been made out in respect to the said loan has been fabricated by the accused No.1-Manager at the Bank and in collusion with accused No.2, who is the petitioner herein and as such, the matter was sought to be referred to the Narcotic and Economic Police Station for investigation, in terms of Section 156 (3) of the Cr.P.C. Vide order dated 7.3.2018 such reference order having been made, the petitioner is before this Court challenging the filing of PCR No.20/2018 as also the order of reference.
4. Sri

.Dhananjay Kumar., learned counsel for the petitioner, would submit that the entire matter is civil in nature inasmuch as there is a loan transaction between the parties, if at all, it is for the Bank to initiate recovery proceedings and not criminal proceedings.

His further submission is that an Smt Girija vs State Of Karnataka on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76539144/
2 earlier NC: 2024:KHC:10270 complaint having been filed in PCR No.33/2018 against the proprietary concern of the petitioner has been dismissed and as such a second complaint cannot be filed.
5.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Sri .T.P.Muthanna., learned counsel for respondent No.2, would however submit that the first complaint having been filed, it was realized that the accused No.1-Manager had also colluded with the accused No.2 and it is in that background that the present complaint has been filed.

Initially, the Bank was under the impression that the fabrication was done only by accused No.2, but now that accused No.1 has also been involved in the said offense, who has been suspended from his services,
the present complaint has been filed.

6. Having heard both the counsel and having perused the documents, it is seen that there are serious allegations which have been made against the collusion between the Manager and the petitioner in NC: 2024:KHC:10270 pursuance of which documents have been fabricated and loan to an extent of Rs.25,00,000/- granted to the petitioner.

7. Whether in fact there is any fabrication or not, whether there is a collusion between the Manager and the petitioner or not can only be ascertained during the course of investigation and for now, it cannot be said that the matter is entirely Civil in nature requiring this Court to excise the extraordinary power under Section 482 of the Criminal Procedure Code.

In that view of the matter,
petition stands dismissed.
8. in view of the dismissal of the main petitioner, pending IA does not survive for consideration.
